components.text: Whether examples of ordinary beginnings warrant the universal causal premise for the beginning of all material reality.
The decisive universalization from familiar beginnings to the beginning of all material reality lacks support.
Whether denying a prior material source improperly treats nothing as an entity or removes the asserted need for a cause.
Whether the material-rearrangement distinction supplies an independent reason for the universal causal premise.
The absence of prior material does not itself eliminate a distinct causal explanation of the universe's beginning.
Whether absence of prior causal powers noncircularly explains why a substance cannot begin without a cause.
Whether correctly paraphrasing nothing supplies the missing noncircular warrant for causal necessity.
Appealing to the absence of prior causal powers presupposes rather than explains why a substance cannot begin uncaused.
The quantificational paraphrase of nothing does not supply the missing reason that a beginning must have a cause.
Whether finite part-whole intuitions legitimately establish that an infinite collection cannot be concretely instantiated.
Finite part-whole intuitions do not defeat actual infinities when consistent equinumerosity principles govern infinite sets.
Whether the varying remainders produced by removing equally infinite groups provide a metaphysical reason to reject concrete infinities.
Variable remainders after removing infinite groups are offered as a further reason to reject concrete actual infinities.
Whether the checkout scenarios invoke a valid single infinity-subtraction operation whose differing results generate contradiction.
Whether Hilbert-style subtraction consequences establish metaphysical impossibility rather than consistent relative complements.
The checkout cases are consistent relative-complement operations, not contradictory instances of a single infinity-minus-infinity result.
Consistent formal representation defeats the claim that the subtraction cases establish metaphysical impossibility by contradiction.
Whether failure to reach the end of an endless upward count entails failure of a beginningless sequence to reach its endpoint.
An endless forward count lacks an endpoint, whereas a beginningless countdown has a terminal point, so the alleged symmetry fails.
Whether each stage of a beginningless countdown can be explained without a first stage or unrestricted ultimate explanation.
Each stage of a beginningless countdown can receive a local predecessor-and-rate explanation without an ultimate starting explanation.
Whether the endpoint asymmetry itself fails for a beginningless sequence ordered toward the present.
Whether predecessor and rate explanations are inadequate without a first or global explanation.
A locally specified infinitely descending causal schedule can generate a global contradiction despite each event's local rule.
The Grim Reaper construction supplies a distinct contradiction-based challenge to certain descending beginningless series.
Whether excluding an infinite regress would also establish that the first member must itself possess the power of the final effect.
The paradox does not establish that a finite terminating causal chain begins with an enormously powerful immediate creator.
Whether a weak initiator and stronger intermediate causes can avoid an absolute first cause with enormous creative power.
Even a mediated series must terminate in an absolute first source responsible for everything downstream.
Whether a finite temporal effect specifically requires personal agency rather than an impersonal indeterministic first cause.
Power and causal firstness do not establish personality when an impersonal indeterministic first cause offers the same timing flexibility.
Whether an impersonal indeterministic nonphysical state plausibly explains why the universe originates at a finite time.
The proposed impersonal alternative lacks a plausible nonphysical model explaining why the universe begins only finitely long ago.
Whether a timeless, changeless, disembodied personal cause can coherently possess the consciousness required by the proposed explanation.
A wholly changeless disembodied mind may be unable to sustain the dynamic character apparently essential to consciousness.
